# nf.particles

The project's particle effects (`particles/<id>/effect.json`): timelines of particles authored in the editor, played at a place by scripts.

A table of functions: call them with a dot.

## Functions {#functions}

### `nf.particles.play(effect, location_or_position, options?)` {#play}

Starts playing an effect at a place, from its first tick. It plays for its `duration` (or, looping, until it's stopped) and belongs to the script that played it: when that script unloads, the effect ends (reason `"unloaded"`). Only players within 32 blocks see it (128 for an emitter with `force`), and of those only `viewers` when given. An effect the project doesn't have, a key `options` doesn't take, or an option out of range is an error, and so is an effect whose file has errors and never had a good version (one that did plays its last good version). More than 1024 effects playing on the server at once is an error too: stop the ones you're done with.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `effect` | `string` | Which effect: its folder name under `particles/`. |
| `location_or_position` | [`Location`](location.md)`\|`[`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where it plays: a `Location`, whose `yaw` and `pitch` turn the effect (nil is 0), or a position in the calling centity's world (the server's first world, in a module or a menu or dialog script). |
| `options` (optional) | [`ParticlePlayOptions`](types.md#particleplayoptions) | Who sees it, how big it is, whether it loops, and what it follows. |

**Returns** [`Effect`](effect.md)`?`: The playing effect, or `nil` when the world isn't loaded.

```lua
assert(this:node("lid")):on("click", function(event)
  nf.task(function()
    local here = this:location()
    local effect = here and nf.particles.play("shockwave", here)
    if effect then
      nf.wait_for(effect, "end")
    end
    this:play_animation("open")
  end)
  event:stop()
end)
```
